input.command:
git checkout -b claude/hitbut-detection -q && python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('dev/requirements/requirements.md')
s = p.read_text()
anchor = "\n## 5. HTTP API"
leaves = """
- `4.7` A stance that deviates from the persona's prevailing position on a subject is found, and the finding carries where it was said and to whom.
  <details><summary>Detail</summary>

  The anomaly. What makes it worth surfacing is not that a position moved but that it moved
  *here* — so a finding without the venue is not a claim anyone can act on, and the store
  refuses one. The comparison is against the persona's own prevailing stance on that
  subject, never against another persona: two people disagreeing is not an inconsistency.
  </details>

- `4.8` A stance series that steps from one level to another yields a trend change reporting the interval the step falls in.
  <details><summary>Detail</summary>

  The change point. A series bounds the change between the last utterance before it and the
  first after it, and no further — a single date would be a claim it cannot support. *Why*
  the position moved is out of scope; a bounded, sourced "between these two dates, this
  moved" is what the corpus can actually say.
  </details>

- `4.9` A series that holds one position, and one too short to have a shape, yield nothing.
  <details><summary>Detail</summary>

  The half that keeps the other two honest. A detector that finds something in every series
  finds nothing: a persona who has been consistent must come back empty, and two or three
  utterances are not a trend however far apart they sit. Silence on a flat series is the
  only evidence that a finding on a moving one means anything.
  </details>
"""
assert s.count(anchor) == 1
p.write_text(s.replace(anchor, leaves + anchor))
PY
node --test dev/requirements/coverage.test.ts 2>&1 | grep -A 5 "leaves with no case" | head -5

Read a stance series for anomalies and change points

Phase 6 of #34. The maths is pure functions over a series with no store and no
model in sight, so a case can plant a step change or an outlier and assert
exactly what comes back.

An anomaly is one utterance out of step, and the finding carries where it was
said and to whom — that it moved *here* is what makes it worth surfacing. A
trend change reports the interval the step falls in, never a date: a series
bounds a move between the last utterance before it and the first after it and no
further. Without both ends dated there is no interval, and since the interval is
the whole claim, there is nothing to record.

Writing the anomaly case found a real gap. The baseline is the median of
everything else, recomputed per candidate, which stops an outlier hiding behind
a baseline it dragged towards itself. But that alone reported every point of a
bimodal series as an anomaly — and a bimodal series is exactly what a trend
change looks like, so one series came back claimed twice in two incompatible
ways. An anomaly now also has to be alone: a candidate that a fraction of the
series keeps company with is a second position the persona holds, not an
utterance out of step.

Writing the trend-change case found another: withUtterance collapsed an explicit
null date into its default, so a case that said the source establishes no date
got one anyway. That is the failure 1.3 and 1.9 exist to prevent, sitting in the
fixtures.

The third leaf is the silence. A detector that finds something in every series
finds nothing, so a flat series, a series too short to have a shape, and a series
that drifts without stepping must all come back empty — verified by slackening
the thresholds and watching that case fail.

Refs #34

input.title: Detection: anomalies and change points over a stance series
input.body:
#34's phase 6. Reading a stance series for the two things it can honestly say.

- **Anomaly** — an utterance out of step with the persona's prevailing position on a subject, carrying the venue and audience it was said to, because that it moved *there* is what makes it worth surfacing.
- **Trend change** — a change point, reported as the interval the step falls in. A series bounds a move between the last utterance before it and the first after it and no further; a date would be a claim it cannot support.
- **Neither** — a flat series, one too short to have a shape, and one that drifts without stepping all come back empty. A detector that finds something in every series finds nothing.

Comparison is always against the persona's own series: two people disagreeing is not an inconsistency.

## Exit

Leaves `4.7`, `4.8`, `4.9`, each with a case over a series whose positions the case itself plants.

Refs #34

input.title: Read a stance series for anomalies and change points
input.head: claude/hitbut-detection
input.body:
Phase 6 of #34. The maths is pure functions over a series — no store, no model — so a case can plant a step change or an outlier and assert exactly what comes back. ## Two things a series can honestly say **An anomaly** is one utterance out of step, and the finding carries the venue and audience it was said to. That it moved *there* is what makes it worth surfacing at all. **A trend change** reports the interval the step falls in, never a date. A series bounds a move between the last utterance before it and the first after it, and no further. With either end undated there is no interval — and since the interval is the whole of the claim, `4.8` proves nothing is recorded rather than something recorded vaguely. ## Two things the cases found **The bimodal problem.** The baseline is the median of *everything else*, recomputed per candidate, which stops an outlier hiding behind a baseline it dragged towards itself. That alone reported **every point of a bimodal series as an anomaly** — and a bimodal series is exactly what a trend change looks like, so one series came back claimed twice, in two incompatible ways. An anomaly now also has to be **alone**: a candidate that a fraction of the series keeps company with is a second position the persona holds, not an utterance out of step. `4.7` asserts the split series produces one trend change and zero anomalies. **The fixture was inventing dates.** `withUtterance` used `options.saidAt ?? default`, so a case saying "the source establishes no date" got one anyway. That is precisely the failure `1.3` and `1.9` exist to prevent, sitting in the fixtures where it would have quietly propped up any case about undated utterances. Now `'saidAt' in options` decides, so an explicit null means it. Neither was something I set out to fix. Both came out of writing the case before believing the code. ## The silence `4.9` is the leaf that keeps the other two honest — a detector that finds something in every series finds nothing. Three series that must come back empty: | series | why it must be silent | |---|---| | holds one position, with ordinary variation | a persona who has been consistent has to come back empty | | three utterances, far apart | two positions are not a trend however different | | drifts steadily from +0.6 to −0.15 | moving gradually is not moving *at a moment*; an interval for it would name two dates that mean nothing | Verified by slackening the thresholds to 0.02/0.03 and watching that case fail — which it did, on the flat series first. ## Folders touched
**`src/backend/detection/`** — new. `series.ts` holds the maths (leave-one-out median baseline, the alone rule, the largest-step change point) and the three named thresholds in one place. `run.ts` turns a stored series into findings and takes no model. **`dev/requirements/`** — leaves `4.7`, `4.8`, `4.9` with their cases, and a `withSeries` fixture that scripts positions and dates outright — a case that plants a step change has to be able to say exactly where it planted it.
## What it deliberately does not do **One change point per pass, not several.** A series with two genuine steps is a persona who moved twice; reporting the larger one leaves the other to be found once the first is accounted for. Reporting both from one pass needs a segmentation this does not do, and claiming it would be claiming something the method cannot support. **The score is a rule of thumb, and says so.** It maps how far the trigger exceeded its bar onto 0–1 so the surfacing threshold has something to compare against. It is not a calibrated probability and the comment refuses to call it one. **Nothing is wired to a scheduled run yet.** Detection needs stances, stances need #27's models. The functions and their proof land now; what calls them lands with phase 5. ## Verification `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (66), `npm run test:server` (12, real workerd), `npm run test:screen` (11). `check_the_world.mjs`: 0 blocking. CI still cannot run — every workflow fails at startup, see #39. Closes #49 Refs #34 --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

content.text:
{"id":5218896773,"number":34,"state":"open","locked":false,"title":"Implement the utterance/stance architecture: ingestion, embeddings, backfill","body":"The tracking issue for the redesign in [`docs/architecture/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/blob/main/docs/architecture/DESIGN.md) (PR pending). The design doc carries the end state and the rationale; this issue carries only the phases and their exit conditions. Append-only once agreed.

**What changed and why.** v1 (#25) shipped a corpus of flat statements judged in pairs against a topic list read off the source. Three things break that at the scale now intended — decades of archives, many sources, a big roster: one speech carried by five outlets became five statements; pairwise judging is O(n²) and cannot see a trend at all; and a topic vocabulary decides in advance what the corpus may be about. The replacement is utterances with many attestations, subjects discovered by embedding, and a stance series per persona per subject.

**This is cheap now and expensive later.** The corpus is fixtures, so this is a rewrite of code and spec, not a migration of cited data. After the first real source it becomes the hard case the stable-id promise exists to prevent.

## Phases

**0. Provisioning (human-only, front-loaded)** — see the comment added to #27
- [ ] Vectorize index created and bound; Workflows enabled on the account.
- [ ] The embedding model and the stance model chosen, both reachable from the Worker.
- [ ] Exit: `wrangler deploy --dry-run` resolves the new bindings from the committed config.

**1. Verify the Workflow bet**
- [ ] Read Cloudflare's published step, duration and payload limits for Workflows and check a one-year archive slice against them. **They could not be read from the session that wrote the design** — the doc says so rather than asserting numbers.
- [ ] Exit: either a slice size that provably fits, or a recorded decision to slice smaller / move the stage.

**2. Spec first**
- [ ] Rewrite the affected leaves in `dev/requirements/requirements.md`: utterance vs attestation, date precision, roster resolution (#31), emergent clusters, stance, the two finding kinds. Watch the coverage gate go red before any case exists.
- [ ] Exit: the gate is red for exactly the new leaves, green once claimed.

**3. Data model**
- [ ] `utterances` + `attestations` replace `statements`; `said_at_precision`; `clusters`, `stances`, `findings`.
- [ ] Exit: logic cases prove one speech across three documents is one utterance and three attestations; that a month-precision date is neither a day nor unknown; that supersede-not-overwrite still holds for findings.

**4. Ingestion**
- [ ] The pipeline as one module — fetch, extract, resolve, merge, embed, assign, stance — every stage idempotent under retry.
- [ ] Exit: behavior cases prove a replayed payload writes nothing new, an unrostered speaker is retained unattributed, and the same quote at three lengths merges to one utterance.

**5. Embedding, clustering, stance**
- [ ] Vector store and stance model behind interfaces a case can script; online cluster assignment; stance stored with model and prompt version.
- [ ] Exit: cases over fixtures where the *source* topic strings deliberately disagree still cluster together (#33), and a scripted stance model produces a readable series.

**6. Detection**
- [ ] Anomaly (deviation from prevailing stance, carrying venue and audience) and trend change (change point, reported as an interval).
- [ ] Exit: cases over a synthetic series with a planted step change and a planted outlier find each, and find nothing in a flat series.

**7. Backfill Workflow**
- [ ] One run per archive slice, sharing the ingestion code, resumable per step.

The design doc carries the end state and the rationale; this issue carries only the phases and their exit conditions. Append-only once agreed.

**What changed and why.** v1 (#25) shipped a corpus of flat statements judged in pairs against a topic list read off the source. Three things break that at the scale now intended — decades of archives, many sources, a big roster: one speech carried by five outlets became five statements; pairwise judging is O(n²) and cannot see a trend at all; and a topic vocabulary decides in advance what the corpus may be about. The replacement is utterances with many attestations, subjects discovered by embedding, and a stance series per persona per subject.

**This is cheap now and expensive later.** The corpus is fixtures, so this is a rewrite of code and spec, not a migration of cited data. After the first real source it becomes the hard case the stable-id promise exists to prevent.

## Phases

**0. Provisioning (human-only, front-loaded)** — see the comment added to #27
- [ ] Vectorize index created and bound; Workflows enabled on the account.
- [ ] The embedding model and the stance model chosen, both reachable from the Worker.
- [ ] Exit: `wrangler deploy --dry-run` resolves the new bindings from the committed config.

**1. Verify the Workflow bet**
- [ ] Read Cloudflare's published step, duration and payload limits for Workflows and check a one-year archive slice against them. **They could not be read from the session that wrote the design** — the doc says so rather than asserting numbers.
- [ ] Exit: either a slice size that provably fits, or a recorded decision to slice smaller / move the stage.

**2. Spec first**
- [ ] Rewrite the affected leaves in `dev/requirements/requirements.md`: utterance vs attestation, date precision, roster resolution (#31), emergent clusters, stance, the two finding kinds. Watch the coverage gate go red before any case exists.
- [ ] Exit: the gate is red for exactly the new leaves, green once claimed.

**3. Data model**
- [ ] `utterances` + `attestations` replace `statements`; `said_at_precision`; `clusters`, `stances`, `findings`.
- [ ] Exit: logic cases prove one speech across three documents is one utterance and three attestations; that a month-precision date is neither a day nor unknown; that supersede-not-overwrite still holds for findings.

**4. Ingestion**
- [ ] The pipeline as one module — fetch, extract, resolve, merge, embed, assign, stance — every stage idempotent under retry.
- [ ] Exit: behavior cases prove a replayed payload writes nothing new, an unrostered speaker is retained unattributed, and the same quote at three lengths merges to one utterance.

**5. Embedding, clustering, stance**
- [ ] Vector store and stance model behind interfaces a case can script; online cluster assignment; stance stored with model and prompt version.
- [ ] Exit: cases over fixtures where the *source* topic strings deliberately disagree still cluster together (#33), and a scripted stance model produces a readable series.

**6. Detection**
- [ ] Anomaly (deviation from prevailing stance, carrying venue and audience) and trend change (change point, reported as an interval).
- [ ] Exit: cases over a synthetic series with a planted step change and a planted outlier find each, and find nothing in a flat series.

**7. Backfill Workflow**
- [ ] One run per archive slice, sharing the ingestion code, resumable per step.
- [ ] Exit: a slice runs end to end against fixtures; a deliberately failed step retries without re-fetching.

**8. API and site**
- [ ] `/api/v1` and the six pages carry utterances, attestations and findings. The inconsistency page keeps its shape: the two representative utterances either side of a change point.
- [ ] Exit: server and screen lanes green; goldens refreshed and reviewed.

input.commit_title: Read a stance series for anomalies and change points (#50)
input.commit_message:
Phase 6 of #34. Pure functions over a series — no store, no model — so a case
can plant a step change or an outlier and assert exactly what comes back.

An anomaly is one utterance out of step, carrying where it was said and to whom.
A trend change reports the interval the step falls in, never a date; without
both ends dated there is no interval and nothing is recorded.

Two things the cases found. The leave-one-out baseline alone reported every point
of a bimodal series as an anomaly — and a bimodal series is what a trend change
looks like — so an anomaly now also has to be alone. And withUtterance collapsed
an explicit null date into its default, which is the failure 1.3 and 1.9 exist to
prevent, sitting in the fixtures.

The third leaf is the silence: a flat series, one too short to have a shape, and
one that drifts without stepping must all come back empty.

Merged without CI verification: GitHub Actions has been failing every run in this
repository at startup since 2026-08-22T00:01Z (see #39). Verified locally
instead — typecheck, 66 default-lane tests, 12 server on real workerd, 11 screen
goldens, and check_the_world at 0 blocking.

Closes #49
Refs #34
